screens.title: Difference arrays
screens.prose: That second list is a **difference array**: cell $i$ holds the change from day $i - 1$ to day $i$. It is the inverse of a prefix sum, from `ds` lesson 7. An update touches two cells, however long its range.

explain.text: The largest index written is $r + 1 = n$, so the list needs $n + 1$ cells. The running total stops at day $n - 1$ and never reads cell $n$. With $l = r$ the $+v$ and $-v$ sit side by side, adding $v$ to that day alone.

screens.title: Solve problem U
screens.prose: Write `apply_ranges(n, updates)` for problem U. Each update is `(l, r, v)`, 0-based and inclusive. Return the list of $n$ final values. Mark both ends of every update, then take one running total.

lines: n days (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10⁵), all 0 at first, and
q updates (1 ≤ q ≤ 10⁵), each l r v:
add v to days l to r (0-based, inclusive).
params.title: Problem U

screens.question: Write `apply_ranges(n, updates)`.

widget.solution:
def apply_ranges(n, updates):
    d = [0] * (n + 1)
    for l, r, v in updates:
        d[l] += v
        d[r + 1] -= v
    out = []
    run = 0
    for i in range(n):
        run += d[i]
        out.append(run)
    return out

byKey.test-2: Test 2 has $l = r = 2$: +7 at cell 2 and −7 at cell 3.
byKey.test-3: Test 3's updates end on the last day. The −v goes in the spare cell $n$, so make the list $n + 1$ long.

screens.title: In two dimensions
screens.prose:
The rule you used: `d[l] += v` and `d[r + 1] -= v`, then a running total.

$$a_i = \sum_{j=0}^{i} d_j$$

On a grid, an update to rows $r_1$ to $r_2$ and columns $c_1$ to $c_2$ marks four corners. Running totals along rows, then down columns, rebuild it.
screens.question: An update covers rows 1 to 2 and columns 1 to 2. Which mark goes at the far corner, row 3 and column 3?

options.text: $+v$: both $-v$ marks reach that corner, so it adds $v$ back

options.why: Then the region beyond both ends would end at $-2v$, not 0. One $+v$ cancels the double subtraction.

options.text: Nothing: it lies outside the block
options.why: Both $-v$ marks spread into that corner after the running totals, so it needs a correction.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Follow where each mark spreads after the two passes.

explain.text: After both passes, each mark spreads to every cell below and to the right of it. The two $-v$ marks both reach the far region, so $+v$ there brings it back to 0. This is inclusion and exclusion on four corners.

screens.title: Positions from fills
screens.prose: A fill on day $t$ changes the position from day $t$ onwards. That is a difference array with no right end. A desk's fills in one stock over a week are listed.

byKey.abs: You added the sale on day 2 instead of subtracting it.

explain.text: The position on day 4 is the running total of fills up to day 4: $300 - 100 + 200 = 400$. An option position has both ends, so exposure starts on the trade date and stops after expiry. Daily exposure across a book of options is a difference array over dates.

formula.name: Difference array
formula.tex: d_l \leftarrow d_l + v,\quad d_{r+1} \leftarrow d_{r+1} - v,\quad a_i = \sum_{j=0}^{i} d_j
formula.note: The inverse of a prefix sum.
